input.quote: Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.
input.rationale: The Agreement imposes no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation on Customer, so the rule sits at the preferred position. § 12.3 affirmatively preserves Customer's freedom to develop, acquire, license, sell or use any product or service and to engage any supplier, and records that Customer has made no exclusivity commitment. A document-wide search for exclusivity language ("exclusive", sole supplier, requirements, "shall not procure from any third party") returns only non-exclusive licence grants (§ 13.1), Vendor's ownership of Deliverables (§ 14.2), exclusive-remedy and exclusive-jurisdiction provisions — none of which restrict Customer's sourcing. § 7.2 (disclose-and-match before engaging another provider) is a right-to-match mechanic that does not prohibit Customer from using an alternative provider once honoured, so it belongs under MFN, not EXCLUSIVITY; § 2.1's take-or-pay volume floor is a minimum-commitment issue and is flagged under MINCOMMIT. No redline proposed under this rule.
